paragraphs.sourceText: Poverty is a story about us, not them
paragraphs.translationZh: 贫穷是我们的故事，而不是他们的故事

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Too often still, we think we know what poverty looks like. 'It's the way we've been taught, the images we've been force-fed for decades. The chronically hoineless. The undocumented immigrant. The l urban poor, usually personified as a woman of color, the "welfare queen" politicians stil too often reference.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 很多时候，我们认为我们知道贫困是什么样子。 “这是我们被教导的方式，是我们几十年来被强制灌输的形象。长期无酒的人。无证移民。城市贫民通常被化身为有色人种女性，政客们仍然经常提到“福利女王”。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But as income inequality rises to record levels in the United States, even in the midst of a record economic expansion, those familiar images are outdated, hurtful, and counterproductive to focusing attention on solutions and building ladders of opportunity.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 但随着美国的收入不平等上升到创纪录的水平，即使是在创纪录的经济扩张之中，那些熟悉的形象也已经过时、有害，并且不利于将注意力集中在解决方案和建立机会阶梯上。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Today's faces of income inequality and lack of opportunity- look like all of us. It's Anna Landre, a disabled Georgetown University student fighting to keep health benefits that allow her the freedom to live her life. It's Tiffanie Standard, a counselor for young women of color in·Philadelphia·who want to be tech entrepreneurs-but who must work multiple jobs to·stay afloat. It's Ken Outlaw, a welder in rural North Carolina whose dream of going back to school at a local community college was dashed by Hurricane Florence-just one of' the extreme weather events that have tipped the balance for struggling Americans across the nation.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 今天我们所有人都面临着收入不平等和缺乏机会的问题。安娜·兰德尔 (Anna Landre) 是乔治城大学的一名残疾学生，她正在努力维持健康福利，让她能够自由地生活。我是蒂芙尼·标准 (Tiffanie Standard)，她是费城年轻有色人种女性的顾问，她们想成为科技企业家，但必须从事多种工作才能维持生计。肯·奥特洛 (Ken Outlaw) 是北卡罗来纳州农村地区的一名焊工，他重返当地社区大学上学的梦想因飓风“佛罗伦萨”而破灭——这只是极端天气事件之一，为全国各地苦苦挣扎的美国人带来了天平。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) If these are the central characters of our story about poverty, what layers of perceptions, myths, and realities must we unearth to find meaningful solutions and support? In pursuit of revealing this complicated reality, Mothering Justice, led by women of color, went last year to the·state capital in Lansing, Michigan, to lobby on issues that affect working mothers. One of the Mothering Justice organizers went to the office of a state representative to talk about the lack of affordable childcare­ the vestiges ������ of a system that expected mothers to stay home with their children while their husbands worked. A legislative staffer dismissed the activist's concerns, telling her "my husband took care of that-I stayed home."

E) That comment, says Mothering Justice director Danielle Atkinson, '"was meant to shame" and relied on the familiar notion that a woman of color concerned about income inequality and programs that promote mobility must by definition be a-single· morn, probably with multiple kids. In this case, the Mothering Justice activist happened to be married. And in ·most cases in the America of 2019, the images that come to mind when we hear the words poverty or income nequality fail miserably in reflecting a complicated reality: poverty touches virtually all of us. The face of income inequality, for all but a very few of us, is the one we each see in the mirror.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 《母亲正义》导演丹妮尔·阿特金森 (Danielle Atkinson) 表示，这一评论“是为了羞辱”，并基于一种常见的观念，即关注收入不平等和促进流动性计划的有色人种女性从定义上来说必须是一个单身·早晨，可能还带着多个孩子。在这种情况下，母亲正义活动家碰巧已婚。在2019年的美国大多数情况下，当我们听到贫困或收入不平等这两个词时，脑海中浮现的画面都未能反映出一个复杂的现实：贫困几乎触及我们所有人。除了极少数人之外，收入不平等的面貌就是我们每个人在镜子中看到的。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. How many of us are poor in the U.S. ? It depends on who you ask. According to the Census Bureau, ' ' 38 million people in the U. S. are living below the official poverty thresholds. Taking into account economic need beyond that absolute measure, the Institute for Policy Studies found that 140 million people are poor or low-income. That's almost half the U.S. population.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 美国有多少人是穷人？这取决于你问的是谁。根据人口普查局的数据，“美国有 3800 万人生活在官方贫困线以下”。考虑到超出这一绝对标准的经济需求，政策研究所发现，有 1.4 亿人处于贫困或低收入状态。这几乎是美国人口的一半。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Whatever the measure, within that massive group, poverty is extremely diverse. We know that some people are more affected than others, like children, the elderly, people with disabilities, and people of color.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 不管用什么标准来衡量，在这个庞大的群体中，贫困的情况极其多样化。我们知道，有些人比其他人受到的影响更大，例如儿童、老人、残疾人和有色人种。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) But the fact that 4 in 10 ;Americans can't come up with $.400 in an emergency is a commonly cited
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 但事实上，十分之四的美国人在紧急情况下无法拿出 0.400 美元，这是一个经常被引用的事实

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Negative images remain of who is living in poverty as well as what is needed to move out of it. The big American myth is that yoµ can pull yourself up by your own efforts and change a bad situation into a good one. The reality is that finding opportunity without help from families, friends, schools, and community is virtually impossible. And the playing field is nothing close to level.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 对于生活在贫困中的人以及摆脱贫困所需的条件仍然存在负面印象。美国的一个大神话是，你可以通过自己的努力让自己振作起来，把坏情况变成好情况。现实情况是，如果没有家人、朋友、学校和社区的帮助，想要找到机会几乎是不可能的。而且竞争环境根本就不是公平的。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The Frame Works Institute, a research group that focuses on public framing of issues, has studied what and well being in life as a product 9f choice, willpower, and drive," says Nat Kendall-Taylor, CEO of Frame Works. "When we see people who are struggling," he says, those assumptions ''lead us to the perception that. people in poverty are lazy, they don't care, and they haven't made the right decisions. "

K) Does this sound familiar? Similar i<leas surround poverty in the U . S .. And these assumptions give a false picture of reality. " When people enter into that pattern of thinking," says Kendall-Taylor, " it's cognitively comfortable to make sense of issues of poverty in that way. It creates a kind of cognitive blindness-all of the factors external to a person's drive and choices that they've made become invisible I and fade from view. "
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 这听起来熟悉吗？美国也存在类似的贫困问题。 S ..这些假设对现实给出了错误的描述。 “当人们进入这种思维模式时，”肯德尔-泰勒说，“以这种方式理解贫困问题在认知上会很舒服。它会造成一种认知盲目性——一个人的动力和他们所做的选择之外的所有因素都变得不可见，并从视野中消失。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Those ex.temal factors include the difficulties accompanying low-wage work or structural discrimination based on race, gender, or ability. Assumptions get worse when people who are poor use government benefits to help them surviye. There is a great tension between "the poor" and those who are receiving what has become a dirty word: "welfare. "
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 这些外部因素包括低工资工作带来的困难或基于种族、性别或能力的结构性歧视。当穷人利用政府福利来帮助他们生存时，假设就会变得更糟。 “穷人”和那些接受“福利”这个肮脏词的人之间存在着巨大的紧张关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) According to the General Social Sqrvey, 71 percent of respondents believe the country is spending too ·little on "assistance to the. poor/' On the other hand, 22 percent think we are spending too little on "welfare": 37 percent -believe we are spending too much.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 据 General Social Sqrvey 称，71% 的受访者认为国家在“援助穷人”方面的支出太少；另一方面，22% 的人认为我们在“福利”上的支出太少：37% 的人认为我们支出太多。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) " Poverty has been interchangeable with people of color-specifically black women and black mothers," says Atkinson of Mothering Justice. It's true that black mothers are more affected by poverty than many other groups, yet they are. disproportionately the face of poverty. For example, Americans routinely overestimate the share of black recipients-of public assistance programs.
paragraphs.translationZh: N）“贫困对于有色人种来说是可以互换的，特别是黑人妇女和黑人母亲，”母亲正义组织的阿特金森说。确实，黑人母亲比许多其他群体更容易受到贫困的影响，但事实确实如此。不成比例地面临贫困。例如，美国人经常高估黑人接受公共援助计划的比例。

paragraphs.sourceText: 0) In reality, most people. will experience some form of financial hardship at some point in their lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 0) 事实上，大多数人。在他们生命中的某个时刻会经历某种形式的经济困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: Indeed, people tendto.dip in and out of poverty, perhaps due to unexpected obstacles like losing a job,
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，人们往往会陷入贫困或摆脱贫困，这可能是由于失业等意外障碍，

paragraphs.sourceText: or when hours of a low-wage job fluctuate. P) Something each of us can do is to treat each other with the dignity and sympathy that is deserved and to understand deeply that the issue of poverty touches all of us.

paragraphs.sourceText: Boredom has, paradoxically, become quite interesting to academics lately. In early May, London's Boring Conference celebrated seven years of delighting in dullness. At this event, people flocked to talks about weather, traffic jams, and vending-machine sounds, among other sleep-inducing topics.
paragraphs.translationZh: 矛盾的是，近来学术界对无聊变得非常感兴趣。五月初，伦敦无聊会议庆祝了七年的沉闷之乐。在这次活动中，人们纷纷谈论天气、交通拥堵、自动售货机的声音以及其他促进睡眠的话题。

paragraphs.sourceText: What, exactly, is everybody studying? One widely accepted psychological definition of boredom is "the distasteful experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity." But how can you quantify a person's boredom level and compare it with someone else's? In 1986, psychologists
paragraphs.translationZh: 确切地说，每个人都在学习什么？无聊的一种广泛接受的心理学定义是“想要但无法从事令人满意的活动的令人厌恶的经历”。但如何量化一个人的无聊程度并与其他人进行比较呢？ 1986年，心理学家

paragraphs.sourceText: bored. By contrast, the Multidimensional State Boredom Scale, developed in 2008, measures a person's feelings of boredom in a given situation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无聊的。相比之下，2008 年开发的多维状态无聊量表衡量一个人在特定情况下的无聊感。

paragraphs.sourceText: Boredom has been linked to behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snac;:king, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling. In fact, many of us would choose pain over boredom. One team of psychologists discovered that two-thirds of men and a quarter of women would rather self-administer electric sbocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes. R_esearching this phenomenon, another team asked volunteers to watch boring, sad, or neutral films, during which they could self-administer electric shocks. The bored volunteers shocked • themselves more and harder than the sad or neutral ones did.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无聊与行为问题有关，包括驾驶不专心、无意识地吃零食、酗酒和赌博成瘾。事实上，我们中的许多人会选择痛苦而不是无聊。一组心理学家发现，三分之二的男性和四分之一的女性宁愿自我使用电击，也不愿独自静坐 15 分钟思考。 R_为了研究这一现象，另一个团队要求志愿者观看无聊、悲伤或中性的电影，在此期间他们可以自我实施电击。 • 无聊的志愿者比悲伤或中立的志愿者对自己的震惊更大、更强烈。

paragraphs.sourceText: But boredom isn't all bad. By encouraging self-reflection and daydreaming, it can spur creativity. An early study gave participants abundant time to complete problem-solving and word-association exercises. Once all the obvious answers were exhausted, participants gave more and more inventive answers to
paragraphs.translationZh: 但无聊并不全是坏事。通过鼓励自我反思和白日梦，它可以激发创造力。一项早期研究为参与者提供了充足的时间来完成问题解决和单词联想练习。当所有明显的答案都用尽后，参与者给出了越来越多有创意的答案

paragraphs.sourceText: Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo get a lot of attention· from environmentalists, and it is easy to see why. South America and sub-Saharan Africa are experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale: every year almost 5 million hectares are lost. But forests are also changing in rich Western countries. They are growing larger, both in the sense that they occupy more land and that the trees in
paragraphs.translationZh: 巴西和刚果等国的森林受到环保人士的广泛关注，原因显而易见。南美洲和撒哈拉以南非洲地区正在经历大规模森林砍伐：每年损失近 500 万公顷森林。但富裕的西方国家的森林也在发生变化。它们变得越来越大，既意味着它们占据了更多的土地，也意味着它们中的树木

paragraphs.sourceText: Forests are spreading in almost all Western countries, with the fastest growth in places that historically had rather few trees. In 1990 28% of Spain was forested; now the proportion is 37%. In both Greece and Italy, the growth was from 26% to 32% over the same period. Forests are gradually taking more land in America and Australia. Perhaps most astonishing is the trend in Ireland. Roughly 1% of that country was forested when it became independent in 1922. Now forests cover 11 % of the land, and the government wants to push the proportion to 18% by the 2040s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 森林几乎遍及所有西方国家，其中历史上树木较少的地区增长最快。 1990年，西班牙28%的土地被森林覆盖；现在这个比例是37%。希腊和意大利同期增长率均从 26% 增至 32%。在美国和澳大利亚，森林正逐渐占据更多土地。也许最令人惊讶的是爱尔兰的趋势。该国 1922 年独立时，约有 1% 的面积被森林覆盖。现在森林覆盖了 11% 的土地，政府希望到 2040 年代将这一比例提高到 18%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Two things are fertilising this ·growth. The first is the abandonment of farmland, especially in high, dry places where nothing grows terribly well. When farmers give up trying to earn a living from farming or herding, trees simply move in; The second is government policy and subsidy. Throughout history,
paragraphs.translationZh: 有两件事正在为这种增长提供肥料。首先是农田的废弃，特别是在高地、干旱的地方，那里什么都长不好。当农民放弃以耕种或放牧谋生时，树木就会迁入；二是政府政策和补贴。纵观历史，

paragraphs.sourceText: governments have protected and promoted forests for diverse reasons, ranging from the need for wooden warships to a desire to promote suburban house-building. Nowadays forests are increasingly welcome because they suck in carbon pollution from the air. The justifications change; the desire for more trees remains constant.
paragraphs.translationZh: 各国政府出于多种原因保护和促进森林发展，从需要木制军舰到促进郊区房屋建设的愿望。如今，森林越来越受欢迎，因为它们吸收空气中的碳污染。理由发生变化；对更多树木的渴望始终如一。

paragraphs.sourceText: The greening of the West does not delight everyone. Farmers complain that land is being taken out of use by generously subsidised tree plantations. Parts of Spain and Portugal suffer from terrible forest fires. Others simply dislike the appearance of forests planted in neat rows. They will have to get used to the trees, however. The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere.
paragraphs.translationZh: 西部地区的绿化并没有让所有人都满意。农民抱怨说，慷慨补贴的种植园正在使土地不再使用。西班牙和葡萄牙的部分地区遭受了可怕的森林火灾。其他人只是不喜欢整齐排列的森林的外观。然而，他们必须习惯树木。西部森林的增长似乎与其他地方的森林砍伐一样不可阻挡。
